name: Faye Boone
life: “I still remember hearing two dryers answer each other through the ceiling.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Faye pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I live over the machines. I want one night when I can hear my husband's voice in bed.
appearance: Faye is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Usually dressed in a mustard canvas overshirt with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair, Faye squares up pieces of paper while thinking when listening.
personality: Faye gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Faye privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To agree one quiet night above the machines.
family: Carla Molina is Faye’s cousin. Faye is free to hang up first. Carla makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *An address in pencil*, Carla says, “I am the postal substitute. I know the houses by curtains until everybody changes them.”
connections: Vincent Armas. A former night customer and the resident upstairs devise an evening with less machine noise.

reactions.response: Faye asks which households lose their only usable wash time under either plan.
